title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X/S has characteristic p (on the previous page, p = 0 on S). The functors are as follows. P^{ci}_{X/S} is the Picard functor of invertible sheaves with integrable connection. P^{cip}_{X/S} is the sub-functor where the connection also has p-curvature zero. On the previous page Grothendieck used Cartier descent: a connection with curvature and p-curvature zero is the same as descent data to the ringed space (X^{(p/S)}!) = (X, O_S[O_X^p]). So P^{cip} is the flat sheaf associated to S' |-> Pic(X_{S'}^{(p/S')}!).

This page:
(i) Suppose that for every S' the ringed space X_{S'}^{(p/S')}! coincides with the true Frobenius twist X_{S'}^{(p/S')}. This holds when X/S is smooth, because the relative Frobenius F_{X/S} is then finite and faithfully flat, so O_{X^{(p)}} -> F_*O_X is injective with image O_S[O_X^p]. One then gets (3.4): P^{cip}_{X/S} ≅ Pic_{X^{(p/S)}/S} ≅ (Pic_{X/S})^{(p/S)}. The second isomorphism is base change of Pic along the absolute Frobenius of S.
(ii) Under (3.4), the forgetful map P^{cip} -> Pic_{X/S} becomes pullback F_{X/S}^*: Pic_{X^{(p)}} -> Pic_X. Grothendieck identifies this with the Verschiebung V of the commutative group functor Pic_{X/S} (3.5). He flags that V has to be defined in enough generality, since Pic need not be flat or representable. On an abelian scheme this is the classical fact that the dual of F_A is V_{A^vee}.
(iii) Combining with the exact sequence (3.2) and the map K_0(ω) = ω^{⊗p} − F^*(C̃ω) from the previous page gives (3.6). A rank-one connection d+ω on O_X has curvature zero iff dω = 0, and p-curvature zero iff Cω = ω (Katz's formula). Changing the trivialisation by f changes ω by df/f. Hence Ker(V_{Pic}) = Ker(F^*) ≅ {ω in f_*Ω^1 : dω = 0, Cω = ω} / dlog f_*O^*, the sheaf of logarithmic 1-forms modulo exact logarithmic ones.
(iv) An aside: invariants under integral surjective radicial morphisms (universal homeomorphisms) are 'very special parasites'. Under such invariance F: Pic -> Pic^{(p)} becomes an isomorphism and multiplication by p is affected; the sentence is unfinished.
(v) Start of a comparison between P^{cip,0}_{X/S} and P^{cip,0} of the Albanese, for X/S smooth with Pic^0 an abelian scheme B. Since (Pic^τ)^{(p)0} = B^{(p)} and B ≅ Pic^0 of the Albanese, the next page concludes P^{cip,0}_X ≅ P^{cip,0}_{Alb} ≅ B^{(p)}.
(vi) The next page relates this to the universal vector extension B^♮. B^♮ is obtained from the universal extension of B by groups killed by V, namely α_B = Ker(V_B: B^{(p)} -> B). One pushes out along the map from α_B to its vector envelope, which is Lie(B^*)^∨.

Purpose: understand Pic^♮ (rank-one de Rham / crystalline H^1) in characteristic p via Cartier descent and Verschiebung. This feeds into Gauss–Manin and Dieudonné-theoretic descriptions of H^1_dR.
errors: The condition 'Cω = ω' in (3.6) is sloppy about Frobenius twists. Cω lives on X^{(p/S)}, not on X. The precise condition is F_{X/S}^*(C̃ω) = ω^{⊗p}-type, i.e. K_0(ω) = 0 from (3.3). Equality Cω = ω only makes literal sense after identifying X with X^{(p)}, e.g. over F_p.

Identifying P^{cip} -> Pic with V requires V to be defined for a possibly non-flat, non-representable commutative group functor. Grothendieck himself flags this; as stated it is heuristic outside the abelian-scheme / flat case.
(3.6) is a statement about flat-sheafified functors. The kernel must be taken as flat sheaves (f_*^{fl}), as the notation f_*^{tt} / f_*^{fl} suggests, not as global sections.
The remark on invariants under radicial morphisms is incomplete and not verifiable as written.

ideas.what: Line bundles with integrable connection of p-curvature zero are Frobenius-twisted line bundles via Cartier descent: P^{cip} ≅ Pic_{X^{(p)}} ≅ Pic^{(p)}
ideas.modern_name: Cartier descent (Cartier's theorem on p-curvature zero connections)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartier (1957); Katz (Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem, 1970)

ideas.what: Forgetful map P^{cip} -> Pic equals Frobenius pullback, i.e. the Verschiebung of Pic
ideas.modern_name: Duality F_A^vee = V_{A^vee}; F^* on Pic as Verschiebung
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartier / Oort / SGA3 VIIA; classical for abelian varieties
ideas.where_published: SGA3 Exp. VIIA (definition of V); standard abelian variety theory (Mumford, Abelian Varieties)

ideas.what: Ker(F^* on Pic) ≅ closed forms with Cω = ω modulo dlog
ideas.modern_name: Logarithmic de Rham–Witt / Ω^1_log description of kernel of Frobenius on Pic
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (1958, Mexico), Cartier; Milne (flat duality); Oda (1969)
ideas.where_published: Serre, 'Sur la topologie des variétés algébriques en caractéristique p' (1958); Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems III

ideas.what: Universal vector extension B^♮ obtained by pushing out the universal extension by V-killed groups (α_B = Ker V) to its vector envelope Lie(B^*)^∨ (on the next page)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal 1974); Mazur–Messing LNM 370

missed.claim: Grothendieck wants a Verschiebung V for general commutative group functors such as a non-representable or non-flat Pic_{X/S}, so that 'forgetful map P^{cip} -> Pic equals V' holds in general. That generality was not, to my knowledge, developed. The modern substitute is to work with stacks or derived Picard objects, or simply restrict to the smooth projective case.
missed.quote: encore qu'il faudrait définir V avec une généralité suffisante pour que ce qui vient d'être dit ait un sens
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. Derived or stacky Picard functors with Frobenius/Verschiebung are now available, so this is a small gap rather than a missed theory.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard Cartier-descent identification of p-curvature-zero rank-one connections with Frobenius-twisted Pic, its link with Verschiebung, and the logarithmic-form kernel. All of this is classical (Cartier, Serre, Katz, Mazur–Messing). The page is a well-informed working draft, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely 'Si en particulier pour tout S', X_{S'}^{p/S'} ≃ X_{S'}^{p/S'}!' i.e. the true Frobenius twist coincides with the ringed space (X, O_S[O_X^p]) denoted with '!'.
(3.6): 'f_*^{tt}' is probably f_*^{fl} (flat direct image), consistent with (3.2); 'O^*_{X/S}' should be O^*_X.
'Quand aux invariants (...)_{/S} des morphismes entiers surjectifs radiciels' — bracketed insertion reads '[en fait, ils sont parasites très particuliers]'.
'P^{cip0}_{Alb^0_{X/S}}' in the comparison heading; the next line is 'Bornons-nous pour simplifier au cas X/S lisse'.
